subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Behavioral Insights in Debt Collection
description: A quick win: understand Behavioral Insights in Debt Collection.

hook.text: A government agency rewrote its debt letter in plain language with a clear action step. Repayment doubled.

buildup.text: Debt collection letters are often legalistic and confusing. Recipients ignore what they can't understand.

discovery.text: Adding a specific repayment plan, like pay $50 monthly starting March 1, increases response rates more than a vague pay.

twist.text: Threatening language often backfires with low-income debtors. It triggers avoidance and shame rather than action.

climax.text: Behavioral debt collection treats debtors as humans, not opponents. Clear language, specific steps, and empathy recover.

punchline.text: A kind letter collects more debt than an angry one.

quiz.question: Why does threatening language backfire in debt collection?
options: It motivates faster repayment through fear
It triggers avoidance and shame rather than action
